newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu vows to continue Jewish settlement.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu vows to continue Jewish settlement.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday ahead of crisis talks in Washington next week that Israel will go on building Jewish settlements on occupied land despite violent Palestinian protests.
"We will continue to build in Jerusalem, also on Har Homa. We will continue to build in settlements -- period," Netanyahu said to members of his right-wing Likud party in Tel Aviv.
Lashing out at the Palestinian Authority, Netanyahu said the self-rule administration had yet to extinguish the "green light for terror" he charged it has given to Moslem militants.
Israel demands Palestinian President Yasser Arafat crack down on "terrorism" as a condition for resuming peace talks.
Palestinians insist peace talks can restart only when Israel halts work on a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on a hill called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.
All eyes have turned to U.S. President Bill Clinton for a new initiative to rescue the U.S.-sponsored Middle East peace process. Clinton has pledged renewed personal involvement.
Before Netanyahu's speech, his spokesman said the prime minister would insist during the U.S. visit on Israel's "right" to settle Jews in East Jerusalem and elsewhere in the West Bank.

In the 15th straight day of West Bank violence since Israel broke ground for the East Jerusalem settlement, Palestinian students in Bethlehem rained stones on Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint while staging a mock funeral for peace.

Protesters set alight a black coffin with a dove and olive branch inscribed with the words "Killed by Netanyahu". Israeli soldiers dispersed the protesters with teargas and rubber bullets. No injuries were reported.
Netanyahu accused the Palestinian Authority of using violence to further its political aims.
"The Palestinian Authority gave the green light for terror, explicitly, about two weeks ago and as a result terror was resumed and the light has yet to change," he said in the Tel Aviv speech.
A Moslem suicide bomber killed three Israeli women in a Tel Aviv cafe on March 21 and two Palestinians died in a botched suicide blasts in Gaza this week.
The military wing of the Islamic Jihad group on Thursday claimed responsibility for the Gaza bombings. Jihad sources said the Palestinian Authority had arrested 30 of their activists.
"They say 'the Jews are building in Jerusalem and that this is bulldozer terror for which we have no other answer'," Netanyahu said.

This, he said, was tantamount to Israel threatening to unleash "Goldsteins to massacre innocent Palestinians unless you accept our specific political demands". U.S.-born settler Baruch Goldstein killed 29 Arabs in a mosque in the West Bank town of Hebron in 1994.

Backing away from enflaming Moslem militants further, Netanyahu's office said Israel had suspended its request the United States extradite Moussa Abu Marzook, a politburo member of the Islamic group Hamas. Abu Marzook said he now expected to be sent to Jordan.
Security sources said Israel feared the extradition would spark attacks and harm its struggle against Islamists.

Netanyahu's office said it was still unclear if Netanyahu, due to meet Clinton at the White House on Monday, would visit Jordan's King Hussein on Sunday in Minnesota where the monarch is to undergo surgery. Earlier, a spokesman for Netanyahu said the Israeli leader would travel to Minnesota.
